definition: The act of giving numerical or statistical form to biological measurements, intensity signals, or cell counts.
etymology: From Latin quantus ('how much') + facere ('to make').
manuscriptExample: Densitometric quantification of Western blot bands was performed across four biological replicates.
conferenceExample: The referee required robust automated image quantification rather than manual spot counting.

definition: To suppress, extinguish, or decrease fluorescence intensity or enzymatic activity rapidly during a assay.
etymology: From Middle English quenchen, from Old English cwencan.
manuscriptExample: Extracellular fluorescence was quenched using trypan blue prior to microplate reader analysis.
conferenceExample: Reviewer 3 queried whether auto-fluorescence background was adequately quenched in tissue sections.
